claim_verdicts.evidence: Hops verified: `.env` holds `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=donhang-dev-password`; docker-compose.yml interpolates it into `PGPASSWORD`; the container prints that value. "The box hands a copy of that environment to every script it runs" is the part that does not hold: a process started by `docker compose exec` has no parent in the box at all — `ps -o ppid -p $$` inside such a process returns 0, and the set it gets is the container's recorded configuration applied by the runtime, not a copy handed down by a box process.

issues.quote: The lab box it starts is a process too, and it starts the scripts you run there.
issues.text: New this round, and not in the claims ledger. Measured: `docker exec donhang-lab ps -eo pid,comm` lists 13 processes (s6-svscan as pid 1, five s6-supervise, sshd.pam, …) — the box is not a process. And it does not start your script: a process created by `docker compose exec` has ppid 0 inside the box (`ps -o pid,ppid -p $$` -> `2602 0`), i.e. no parent there at all; its set is the container's recorded configuration applied by the runtime. Section 5's "the box hands a copy of its own set to every script it runs" and section 4's "the box then hands a copy" repeat it.
issues.fix: Stop calling the box a process. Section 2: "The lab box it starts is a small Linux machine of its own, and every script you run there runs inside it." Section 4: "…then creates the box with that value already in the box's set; every command started in the box afterwards is given a copy of that set." Section 5, last sentence: "…it was put into the box's set when the box was created, and every script started in the box is given a copy." Add a claim for the container hop, separate from the parent-child claim 3.

issues.quote: `${DONHANG_MISSING:-nothing}` supplies a fallback when nothing was handed in — the same idea as `??` in the sample.
issues.text: The equivalence is unlisted and inexact. The permitted mirror documents two forms: "`${VAR:-default}` -> value of `VAR` if set and non-empty, otherwise `default`" and "`${VAR-default}` -> value of `VAR` if set, otherwise `default`". The colon form in the script also fires when the name was handed in but is empty, whereas `??` fires only on `null` ("returns the value of its left-hand operand if it's not `null`", claim 8). `${VAR-word}` is the form that matches `??`, and the script does not use it.
issues.fix: Drop the equivalence or condition it: "…supplies a fallback when the name has no value — a fallback like the `??` in the sample, although this shell form also uses it when the name was handed in empty." Add the wording to claim 13 so the ledger carries the condition.

It is true — output line 2 prints `hello` (the value `env` handed the child), not `xin chào` (the caller's value), which can only happen if the inner `sh` did the expansion — but the author states it without recording it.
issues.fix: Add a claim: "`sh -c 'text'` runs `text` as the started shell's own input, so a name inside single quotes is read by that shell out of the copy it was handed, not by the shell that typed the line." Evidence: env-demo.sh line 10 and output line 2 at stage-0.
